title: Complementary ecosystem services provided by pest predators and pollinators increase quantity and quality of coffee yields
authors: Classen A, Peters MK, Ferger SW, Helbig-Bonitz M, Schmack JM, Maassen G, Schleuning M, Kalko EKV, Bohning-Gaese K, Steffan-Dewenter I
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
location: Southern slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro, Tanzania, 1120-1660 m.a.s.l.
design: Full-factorial 2×2 design: vertebrate exclosure (2×2×2m net cubes, 30×30mm mesh) × pollinator exclosure (gauze bags, 0.39×0.77mm mesh on individual twigs). 3 coffee production systems: homegardens (HOM, ~80% canopy), shaded plantations (SHA, ~30% canopy), sun plantations (SUN, full sun). 4 sites per production system = 12 sites total. 3 clusters of 4 bushes per site. Total = 180 bushes. September 2011–November 2012. GLMM with site/cluster/bush/twig as nested random effects. Pollinator exclosures removed 1 week after blossom to allow normal herbivore access.
notes: 12 study sites (4 per production system) is the highest-level replicate. Within each site, 3 clusters × 4 treatments = 12 bushes. This is a 2×2 factorial (VertEx × PollEx), so the vertebrate exclusion effect is tested across all pollinator treatments and vice versa. The simplified model retained only VertEx for fruit set and only PollEx for fruit weight — no interactions were significant. Vertebrate exclosure excludes both birds and bats (30mm mesh). The text reports average effects: 9.0% reduction in late fruit set from vertebrate exclusion, 7.4% reduction in fruit weight from pollinator exclusion. No raw group means are tabulated — only model output (Table 1) and Figure 2. Herbivory increased under vertebrate exclosures (Fig 3a) but coffee berry borer infestation was unaffected (1.53% average). The pollinator exclusion effect (fruit weight) is not directly relevant to the predator-exclusion PICO but is recorded for completeness as it affects yield quality.

observations.tissue: fruit set (late fruit set = harvestable fruits / flowers)
observations.data_source: Text p3 (Section 3 Results); Table 1 (simplified model: VertEx χ²=4.89, P=0.027); Fig. 2a, PDF page 5
observations.treatment_description: vertebrate exclosure — 2×2×2m cultivation guard net cubes (30×30mm mesh) excluding birds and bats from whole coffee bushes for 6+ months
observations.control_description: open control — coffee bushes fully accessible to flying vertebrates (birds and bats), no netting

figure_read.structure: Panel (a): 3 groups on x-axis (HOM, SHA, SUN). 4 bars per group representing 4 treatments (open control, pollinator exclosure, vertebrate exclosure, combined exclosure). Y-axis 'late fruit set (%)' with broken axis: 0, then fissure, then 20-70%; ticks at 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70; spacing 10; linear. Bar colors indicate lumping by VertEx in simplified model (dark = vertebrate-accessible, light = vertebrate-excluded). No error bar type stated in caption; likely SE or 95% CI from the GLMM.
figure_read.evidence_note: Fig 2a p5; broken y-axis (fissure at ~20%) makes precise calibration unreliable. 12 bars total (4 per production system) are closely packed. Overall pattern: vertebrate-accessible bars consistently taller than vertebrate-excluded bars across all 3 production systems. Approximate reads: HOM open ~45%, HOM VertEx ~38%; SHA open ~45%, SHA VertEx ~42%; SUN open ~53%, SUN VertEx ~48%. But broken axis and crowded bars prevent reliable digitization. Text states 9.0% average reduction, which is the authoritative number.

observations.notes: Raw means not reported in text or tables. The 9.0% reduction is the model-estimated average effect across all production systems and pollinator treatments. From GLMM: simplified model VertEx χ²=4.89, P=0.027. No VertEx × production system interaction (χ²=3.91, P=0.142). Vertebrate exclusion also increased herbivory rates (Fig 3a, significant in HOM and SUN). Mechanism: increased herbivory triggers resource reallocation from reproductive to vegetative organs, plus possible increase in sap-sucking insects.

observations.tissue: fruit weight (berry weight as quality/yield proxy)
observations.data_source: Text p4 (Section 3 Results); Table 1 (simplified model: PollEx F₁,₈₃=8.93, P=0.004); Fig. 2b, PDF page 5
observations.treatment_description: pollinator exclosure — transparent gauze bags (0.39×0.77mm mesh) over individual twigs excluding insect pollinators during flowering; removed 1 week after blossom
observations.control_description: open pollinated twigs — insects (honeybees A. mellifera, wild bees, syrphids, butterflies) had full access to coffee flowers

moderators.predator_group: insect pollinators (not predators — this is the pollination treatment)

figure_read.structure: Panel (b): 3 groups (HOM, SHA, SUN). Y-axis 'fruit weight (g)' with broken axis: 0, then fissure, then 1.2-1.7g; ticks at 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7; spacing 0.1. Bars lumped by PollEx in simplified model (dark = open pollinated, light = pollinator excluded).
figure_read.evidence_note: Fig 2b p5; broken y-axis and 12 crowded bars. Approximate: HOM open ~1.42g, PollEx ~1.30g; SHA open ~1.55g, PollEx ~1.45g; SUN open ~1.50g, PollEx ~1.40g. Overall open ~1.49g, PollEx ~1.38g. (1.38-1.49)/1.49 = -7.4%, consistent with text. Precise digitization not possible due to broken axis and bar density.

observations.notes: This observation records the POLLINATOR exclusion effect on fruit weight, NOT the vertebrate/predator exclusion effect. Vertebrate exclusion had NO effect on fruit weight (F₁,₉₀=0.13, P=0.724). This is recorded because fruit weight is a yield-quality component that contributes to total coffee yield, but the manipulated agent is pollinators not predators. For the predator-exclusion PICO, only the fruit set observation (obs 1) is directly relevant. The 7.4% is the model-estimated average across all production systems and vertebrate treatments.

observations.data_source: Fig. 3a, PDF page 6; text p3-4; electronic supplementary material S4b
observations.treatment_description: vertebrate exclosure — 2×2×2m net cubes excluding birds and bats
observations.control_description: open control — vertebrates had full access

figure_read.structure: Bar chart: 3 groups (HOM, SHA, SUN). 2 bars per group: dark = open control, light = vertebrate exclosure. Y-axis 'herbivory (%)' from 0 to 2.0; ticks at 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0.
figure_read.evidence_note: Fig 3a p6; herbivory was higher under vertebrate exclosures than controls in HOM and SUN but not SHA. Bars are small relative to axis range and differences are subtle. Approximate: HOM control ~0.6%, HOM VertEx ~1.0%; SHA control ~0.5%, SHA VertEx ~0.5%; SUN control ~0.3%, SUN VertEx ~0.8%. Text states the interaction VertEx × production system was significant for herbivory after 6 months. Precise values not recoverable.

observations.notes: Herbivory was significantly higher under vertebrate exclosures in HOM and SUN after 6 months (VertEx × production system interaction significant; see ESM S4b). Before exclosure installation, herbivory did not differ between treatment groups. This confirms that vertebrate exclusion increases herbivory — the mechanistic pathway linking predator exclusion to reduced fruit set. No overall mean difference reported in text; only per-production-system in Fig 3a with interaction. Coffee berry borer (H. hampei) infestation was NOT affected by any treatment (average 1.53%).
